PNG gradient export verification: For gradient-export tasks, derive expected canvas size independently from the source artifact and sample multiple vertical bands to check direction, approximate endpoint colors, and absence of unrelated content rather than only checking top and bottom means loosely.
PNG linear gradient verification: For linear gradient exports, verify more than top and bottom averages: sample multiple horizontal bands, check monotonic luminance progression from top to bottom, and check left-to-right uniformity within bands to reject two-color banded fills.
plain-text exact line count: When an instruction requires exactly two lines, evaluate physical lines after normal newline normalization rather than filtering to non-empty lines, otherwise files with extra blank lines can incorrectly pass.
solid-color PNG export verification: For solid-fill image tasks, sparse pixel sampling is weak; use image extrema, histogram, or full pixel scan to ensure the whole canvas has the required RGB value, and verify Image.format is PNG when PNG export is required.

For a required solid fill, do not rely only on center pixel and average color; gate on exact dimensions and verify pixel extrema or all-pixel deviation from the target color within tolerance, otherwise patterned/non-uniform images can falsely pass.
PNG solid-fill verification: For a task requiring an exact solid RGB fill, verify every pixel has exactly the requested RGB values and also check alpha/opacity or mode handling; converting RGBA to RGB can hide fully or partially transparent pixels.
dependency-chain source parsing: Do not award independent rule credit for static source/input files that exist before the task; parse them only to compute expected output values, otherwise preflight can get positive reward without user action.
PNG solid-fill export verification: For Krita canvas-export tasks, robust rule checks should inspect the exported PNG's actual image dimensions, format, and pixel uniformity rather than relying on file existence or visual-only checks.
PNG export validation: When verifying a PNG, inspect Image.format before calling convert(), because PIL conversions may drop the original format metadata; do not rely on the filename extension alone.
dependency-chain verification: Avoid separate rule items that only verify static source-file facts, such as a blend object having vertices; they are user-independent and can inflate reward without proving task completion.
PNG export with solid background: When verifying a solid-background PNG export, treat actual PNG format and opaque alpha as hard gates; transparent black pixels can otherwise pass RGB-only black checks while not representing a solid black canvas.
PNG canvas verification: For exported canvas tasks, required fill color should be a hard gate; avoid awarding high partial credit for correct dimensions when the fill/background is wrong.
large image pixel checks: When expected dimensions may be very large, prefer PIL extrema/histogram or bounded sampling over converting the entire image to a NumPy array to reduce evaluator memory risk.
dependency grounding source files: Do not award task reward for checking immutable source file properties; source grounding checks that are already true initially cause positive initial reward and should be used only to derive expected constants or as non-scoring sanity checks.
gradient PNG verification: A gradient verifier should check all RGB channels and grayscale neutrality, not only one channel, otherwise a single-channel color gradient can falsely pass as black-to-white.
linear gradient PNG verification: For gradient exports, checking only edge colors and horizontal direction is insufficient; add column-wise monotonicity and approximate linearity checks to reject hard split fills or non-smooth gradients.
